attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Kansas office must register to perform attest services for a Kansas client; there is no exemption for this. It may perform non-attest services for a Kansas client without registering if the work is done through an individual with practice privileges under K.S.A. 1-322(a). Dual-sourced: statute + KS Board out-of-state firm registration guidance.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Any firm with a Kansas office practicing CPA accountancy must register -- unqualified by service type or CPA-title use.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board may require peer review as a condition of firm-registration renewal for firms providing attest services, at least once every 3 years; noncompliance is grounds for discipline. Waiver available if no attest services in preceding 12 months.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Kentucky office that is licensed and in good standing in its home state, and compliant with peer review where applicable, is exempt from Kentucky firm licensing for attest and non-attest work.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Qualified trigger: KY office performing attest OR KY office using 'CPA' title triggers licensure -- near-universal in practice since most firms use CPA in their name.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms performing audits/reviews/compilations must enroll in approved peer review; renewal requires proof of current enrollment and most recent report within 3 years.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Louisiana office may perform attest services without a Louisiana permit if non-CPA owners hold only a minority interest, the firm is enrolled and current in peer review, and it is licensed in its home state.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Qualified trigger: LA office providing attest services OR using CPA title requires a firm permit.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms providing attest services (excluding PCAOB-permanent-inspection engagements) must enroll in/comply with board-approved peer review; results reportable to board; annual permit renewal.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Maine office needs a Maine license to perform audit, examination or other services in section 12201(3-A)(A), (C) or (D) for a client with its home office in Maine, unless it qualifies for a firm license under subsections 3 and 8 and works through an individual with practice privileges, or it meets the substantial-equivalency requirements of section 12253 (section 12252(1)(A)(3)). Review and compilation engagements and SSAE examination, review and agreed-upon-procedures engagements (section 12201(3-A)(B), (F)) carry the same two alternative conditions (section 12252(1)(B)), and non-attest services under the CPA title require section 12253 or work through a practice-privilege individual (section 12252(1)(C)). Whether your firm qualifies turns on those conditions; confirm with the board.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A firm must hold a Maine license if it has a Maine office performing any of the services in section 12201(3-A)(A)-(D), or a Maine office that uses the title 'CPA' or 'CPA firm' (section 12252(1)(A)).

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition of granting or renewing a firm license, a firm that provides attest services other than compilations must participate in an approved peer review program: a review within 18 months of initial licensure, then every 3 years (section 12252(8)).

attest_exemption.citation: Md. Code, Bus. Occ. & Prof. section 2-401
attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Maryland office may perform attest services without a Maryland permit if it meets the peer review and application requirements of sections 2-402 to 2-403 and 2-4A-02 and works through an individual with Maryland practice privileges. Non-attest work under the CPA title is likewise exempt when performed through an individual with practice privileges.

physical_office_trigger.citation: Md. Code, Bus. Occ. & Prof. section 2-401(a)
physical_office_trigger.notes: Qualified trigger: MD office performing attest services OR MD office using CPA/CPA-firm title requires a permit.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Md. Code, Bus. Occ. & Prof. Title 2, Subtitle 4A; COMAR 09.24.06
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms performing audit/attest engagements must undergo peer review at least every 3 years under an approved program; permit holders certify peer-review status at each renewal. Not required for non-attest-only firms.

attest_exemption.notes: Section 34-1-16's chapeau bars a firm 'with an office in this state' from providing attest services/using CPA title unless registered. Board's own rule (r. 30-X-3-.04): 'No firm or office not located in this state...shall be required to register as a firm with this Board.' Nonresident CPAs may render non-attest services without notice/fee (section 34-1-7).

physical_office_trigger.notes: Each office established/maintained in Alabama for public accounting practice must register.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Fetched directly: each Practice Unit must undergo peer review at least every 3rd fiscal year; missing the deadline means the permit 'shall not be renewed for the current fiscal year.'

attest_exemption.notes: Alaska's statute and its board regulation give opposite answers for attest work by a firm with no Alaska office. Under AS 08.04.420(d), a firm that is more than one-half owned by CPAs in good standing, has its principal place of business in another state and has no Alaska office may practice in Alaska under a firm practice privilege, and AS 08.04.565(2) allows attest work through such a firm. AS 08.04.420(c) says no notice, fee or documentation is required. The former out-of-state attest permit in AS 08.04.240(k) was repealed effective January 1, 2026. The board regulation 12 AAC 04.245(a)(2) has not been updated and still says a firm with no Alaska office must obtain a permit to provide attest functions under AS 08.04.240(k). Non-attest work by such a firm needs no permit under either source.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A firm with an Alaska office needs an Alaska firm permit. The firm practice privilege in AS 08.04.420(d) covers only a firm with no office in the state.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board may require peer review as a condition of firm-permit renewal, not more than once every 3 years. Corroborated by renewal-instructions PDF requiring the most recent peer-review acceptance report attached.

alaska.source_disagreement: Alaska statute AS 08.04.420(d) and AS 08.04.565(2) let a firm with no Alaska office, whose principal place of business is in another state and which is more than one-half owned by CPAs in good standing, perform attest work under a firm practice privilege with no permit, notice or fee. The out-of-state attest permit in AS 08.04.240(k) was repealed effective January 1, 2026. The board regulation 12 AAC 04.245(a)(2) has not been updated and still requires a permit for attest work by a firm with no Alaska office. Confirm with the Alaska Board of Public Accountancy before performing attest work for an Alaska client without a permit.

attest_exemption.notes: Broader than the typical split: a no-AZ-office firm may practice, INCLUDING attest, without registration if owned/employing a limited-reciprocity-privilege holder in good standing at home. A.R.S. section 32-731 requires attest/compilation 'only through a registered firm' for firms that fall within the registration net otherwise (AZ office or don't meet the exemption conditions). Section 32-731(A) opens 'Except as provided in section 32-725, subsection G' -- an express statutory carve-out, not an inference. Section 32-731(B)'s second sentence independently confirms it, naming a 32-725(G)-qualified individual as a valid signer for attest/compilation reports.

physical_office_trigger.notes: No-AZ-office is a mandatory exemption condition; having an AZ office disqualifies the exemption and triggers section 32-730 biennial registration.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Ariz. Admin. Code R4-1-454; A.R.S. section 32-731
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Peer-review results required for new firm applications and reinstatement; less directly confirmed for ordinary biennial renewal specifically.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Arkansas office must register to perform attest services for a client headquartered in Arkansas. A no-office firm may provide non-attest services, and use the CPA title, without registering if the work is done through a practice-privilege individual and the firm meets peer-review and home-state licensing requirements. Dual-sourced (statute + independent summary).

physical_office_trigger.notes: AR office practicing public accounting or using CPA/CPA-firm title must register, independent of the no-office attest/non-attest split.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Licensees issuing attest reports must enroll in approved peer review; Rule 20 requires submitting peer-review documents within 30 days of notice or with renewal application, whichever first.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm may perform an audit or review for a California-headquartered entity only if it is registered under section 5096.12. An out-of-state individual with a practice privilege may perform non-attest services without a California license or firm registration. The California Board of Accountancy's guidance for out-of-state firm registrants says the same.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Practice-privilege holder barred from providing services 'from any office located in this state' except as an employee of a CA-registered firm -- opening a CA office forces registration regardless of service type.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: To renew/convert to active registration status, a firm must have a peer review report accepted by a board-recognized program no less than every 3 years -- explicit renewal condition, corroborated by a CBA peer-review overview PDF.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm needs a South Dakota permit to do attest work for South Dakota clients, whether or not it has an office in South Dakota. A firm with no South Dakota office may do non-attest and compilation work without a permit if the work is done through a practice-privileged individual.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Office triggers the permit requirement combined with attest services OR restricted CPA/PA title use from that office -- near-universal in practice since almost all firms use the restricted title.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board may require peer review by rule as a condition of firm-permit renewal; SD Board's peer review guidance confirms implementation for financial-reporting-scope firms (1 year after starting, every 3 years thereafter).

attest_exemption.notes: A firm must hold a permit to provide attest services or to use the titles 'CPAs', 'CPA firm', 'PAs' or 'PA firm' (section 62-1-108(a)). The section does not separately address a firm with no Tennessee office performing attest work for a Tennessee client; confirm with the board.

physical_office_trigger.notes: The board grants permits to firms originally licensed in another state that establish an office in Tennessee, and a firm with multiple locations must obtain a permit for each location in Tennessee (section 62-1-108(a), (e)).

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Enrollment in an approved peer review program is a condition for renewal of a permit for firms that issue attest work (Rule 0020-06-.04(1)), and a firm permit application must state the firm's peer review program with proof of compliance (Rule 0020-01-.11(3)(j)).

attest_exemption.notes: Since HB 1520 (effective September 1, 2019), a firm with no Texas office does not need a Texas firm license for attest or non-attest services if the engagement is performed through a Texas-licensed individual or an individual with practice privileges, and the firm submits to the Texas Board's jurisdiction and its ownership and peer review rules. A Texas office is the only unconditional trigger for a firm license.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A firm must hold a firm license if it establishes or maintains a Texas office -- unconditional, independent of service mix.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: A firm subject to peer review cannot have its office license renewed unless peer review requirements are met. Narrow exemptions for PCAOB-only-inspected firms or SSARS-only firms (must request exemption at renewal).

attest_exemption.citation: Utah Admin. Code R156-26a-305(3), as amended by Filing No. 58008 (published Utah State Bulletin, June 1, 2026; effective July 8, 2026 per the Bulletin of July 15, 2026); Utah Code section 58-26a-305(1)(a)
attest_exemption.notes: A CPA firm not licensed in Utah may perform attest or non-attest services in Utah through mobility without a Utah license if its principal place of business is not in Utah and it meets the other conditions of Rule R156-26a-305(3), including Utah's ownership requirement (section 58-26a-302(3)(a)(iii)) and peer review requirement (Rule R156-26a-303a). The rule was amended effective July 8, 2026, after 2025 legislation (SB 15, effective July 1, 2026) rewrote section 58-26a-305(1)(a) to refer only to individuals. Otherwise a firm must register with the Division to engage in the practice of public accounting in Utah (section 58-26a-301(2)).

physical_office_trigger.notes: A firm may not use the title 'certified public accountant' or 'CPA' unless each of its Utah offices is registered with the division (section 58-26a-501(1)(b)), and each separate Utah location of a firm seeking registration must register separately (section 58-26a-302(3)(b)).

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Utah Admin. Code R156-26a-303a, as amended by Filing No. 58008 (published Utah State Bulletin, June 1, 2026; effective July 8, 2026 per the Bulletin of July 15, 2026)
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: A firm engaged in the practice of public accounting must undergo a peer review at least once every three years; a firm outside the peer review requirement must notify the Division of its exemption when it renews its registration (Rule R156-26a-303a, as amended effective July 8, 2026).

attest_exemption.notes: Registration required for a VT-office firm (practicing/using CPA titling), and for a no-office firm performing attest-type services for a VT-home-office client. No-office firm performing non-attest/limited categories for a VT-home-office client is exempt, subject to ownership/practice-privilege conditions. 26 V.S.A. 74(a)-(b): (a)(1)-(2) office-based triggers, (a)(3) the no-office attest trigger for a VT-home-office client, (b) the no-office non-attest exemption.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Registration required if the firm has an office established/maintained in Vermont for public accounting practice -- unconditional on specific service mix once a VT office exists.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: 26 V.S.A. section 75; VT Board Admin Rule 10.7
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board may require peer review as a renewal condition, no more than every 3 years; Rule 10.7 requires an attestation of peer review within the preceding 3 years in the renewal application. Firms with no attest services aren't required to undergo peer review.

attest_exemption.citation: 252 CMR 2.13; Mass. Gen. Laws c. 112, section 87D(a)
attest_exemption.notes: Only a person or firm holding a valid Massachusetts license may issue an audit, review or compilation report, but that bar does not apply to an individual practicing under the section 87B(h)(2) mobility provision (section 87D). Under 252 CMR 2.13, an out-of-state firm cannot enter Massachusetts under section 87B(h)(2) to provide 'restricted services', meaning services its home state's board restricts for Massachusetts CPAs, and a firm whose home board requires firm registration for such services must obtain a Massachusetts license. How this applies depends on your home state's rules; confirm with the board.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A firm applying for or renewing a Massachusetts permit must register each of its Massachusetts offices with the board (section 87B1/2(c)). The statute's licensing triggers are issuing reports and using the CPA title (section 87D), not having an office as such; confirm with the board whether your office's work falls within them.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition of license renewal, a licensee must certify that its practice unit completed, within the preceding three years, a quality review accepted by a report acceptance body (252 CMR 2.15(2)(a)). A practice unit that conducted no attest or compilation engagements in those three years may instead certify that, and must undergo a review within eighteen months of undertaking one.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Michigan office may perform reviews, compilations, examinations and agreed-upon procedures (section 728(4)), or audits and other attest services while using the CPA firm title (section 728(5)), without a Michigan license only if it works through an individual with Michigan practice privileges, is authorized to perform those services where that individual has a principal place of business, and meets the ownership and supervision requirements of section 728(2)(a)-(b) and the peer review requirement of section 729(2). A firm that does not meet every condition must be licensed.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A firm that establishes or maintains an office in Michigan must obtain a Michigan license to practice public accounting in Michigan (section 728(1)).

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: A firm that performs audits, reviews, or compilations relied on by third parties must undergo peer review (section 729(2)). A renewal applicant submits proof of peer review obtained within the preceding 3 years (section 729(3)) and must notify the department within 30 days of a fail rating or a second consecutive pass-with-deficiencies rating (section 729(4)).

attest_exemption.citation: Minn. Stat. section 326A.05, subd. 1(a)(4) and subd. 1(b)-(c)
attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Minnesota office needs a Minnesota permit to perform, for a client headquartered in Minnesota, an audit or other engagement under Statements on Auditing Standards, an examination of prospective financial information, or a PCAOB engagement (subd. 1(a)(4), with section 326A.01, subd. 2, clauses (1), (4), (5)). A firm holding a valid permit from another state may perform government-auditing-standards engagements, PCAOB engagements and compilations for such a client without a Minnesota permit only if it meets the subd. 3(b) ownership requirements, its home state requires equivalent peer review for permit renewal, and it works through an individual with practice privileges under section 326A.14 (subd. 1(b)). The statute lists PCAOB engagements in both paragraphs; confirm with the board. Other services under the CPA title are governed by subd. 1(c).

physical_office_trigger.notes: A firm with a Minnesota office that performs attest services or uses the title 'CPA' or 'CPA firm' must hold a permit, as must one with a Minnesota office that performs compilations to the extent section 326A.10(k) requires (section 326A.05, subd. 1(a)(1)-(3)).

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition of permit renewal, the board by rule requires firms to undergo peer review no more often than once every three years, in a manner the board specifies (section 326A.05, subd. 8(a)).

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Mississippi office needs a Mississippi permit to perform a financial statement audit or other engagement under Statements on Auditing Standards, an examination of prospective financial information, or a PCAOB engagement for a client whose home office is in Mississippi (section 73-33-1(3)(a), with section 73-33-17(4)). It may perform reviews and compilations without a permit only if it has the subsection (4) ownership qualifications, complies with the board's peer review rules, and works through an individual with practice privileges under section 73-33-17 (section 73-33-1(3)(b)). HB 1137 (2026), effective July 1, 2026, changed the education and experience requirements for those individual practice privileges.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Any firm with a Mississippi office that practices public accountancy or uses the title 'CPA' or 'CPA firm' must hold a permit (section 73-33-1(3)(a)).

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Miss. Code Ann. section 73-33-1(3)(b); Miss. State Board of Public Accountancy Rule 5.3.2
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Reviews and compilations by a no-office firm are permitted only if the firm complies with the board's peer review rules (section 73-33-1(3)(b)). Under Board Rule 5.3.2, each ongoing practice unit, other than one that performed no accounting or auditing engagements in the 12 months before registration (Rule 5.3.1), must complete a peer review once every three years in order to register with the board.

attest_exemption.citation: RSMo section 326.289.1(1)-(3), as re-enacted by HCS SS#2 SB 1233 (2026), effective 2026-08-28
attest_exemption.notes: Under RSMo section 326.289.1 as re-enacted by SB 1233 (2026), effective August 28, 2026, a firm with no Missouri office may offer attest and compilation services without a permit if it meets the qualifications of subsection 4(1), complies with peer review requirements, works through an individual with practice privileges under section 326.283, and can lawfully perform those services in that individual's home state. Non-attest services under the CPA title are separately allowed through an individual with practice privileges.

physical_office_trigger.citation: RSMo section 326.289.1(1)(a)-(b), as enacted by HCS SS#2 SB 1233 (2026)
physical_office_trigger.notes: Any firm with an MO office offering attest/compilation services, or using CPA/CPA-firm titling, must hold a permit -- effectively universal for MO-office CPA-titled firms.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: RSMo section 326.289.9, as enacted by HCS SS#2 SB 1233 (2026)
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board required by rule to make peer review (no more than once every 3 years) a condition of permit renewal -- carried forward from the pre-08-28 version with minor wording changes ('comparable' replacing 'substantially equivalent'), core peer-review-renewal linkage preserved.

attest_exemption.notes: Any firm engaged in Puerto Rico in the practice of public accounting must register with the Junta as a firm of public accountants (Seccion 5(a)), and the practice of public accounting is defined as attest services (Seccion 18(12)). The practice-privilege provision of Seccion 4(a) applies to individuals ('persona natural'), not firms, and an individual practicing under it may perform attest services for an entity headquartered in Puerto Rico only through a firm holding a permit (Seccion 4(a)(3)). So attest work in Puerto Rico requires firm registration even without a Puerto Rico office. Services outside the Seccion 18(12) definition, such as tax preparation, consulting and bookkeeping, do not by themselves trigger registration, but a firm may not use the title 'contadores publicos autorizados' or 'CPAs' unless it is registered under Seccion 5 (Seccion 11(b)).

physical_office_trigger.notes: Registration turns on engaging in Puerto Rico in the practice of public accounting (Seccion 5(a)), not on having an office. An office appears only as a condition: each resident manager in charge of a firm office in Puerto Rico must be a Puerto Rico-licensed CPA or public accountant (Seccion 5(a)(4)).

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Renewal of an individual CPA license is conditioned on continuing education evidence (Seccion 6(b)); the statute, as amended through Ley 174-2025, contains no peer review requirement for firms.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm needs a Guam Firm Permit to Practice to provide attest services or to use the CPA or CPA-firm title. Non-attest services without the CPA title fall outside the permit requirement.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Applications must list Guam office addresses/CPAs in charge, and establishing a Guam office is described in secondary sources as one route to a permit, but no provision found stating a bare Guam office alone (absent attest/CPA-title use) independently forces registration. Genuinely unclear.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Explicit: Firm Permit renewal requires enrollment in/completion of board-approved peer review for attest-service firms, with a 3-year lookback exemption for firms already reviewed under an equivalent program. Noncompliance is an enforcement ground.

attest_exemption.citation: 27 V.I.C. section 250d(a)(1)(C), (a)(2)-(3) (Public Accountancy Act of 2014, Act No. 7596)
attest_exemption.notes: Under section 250d(a)(1)(C), a firm with no Virgin Islands office must hold a permit to perform attest services for a client whose home office is in the Virgin Islands; there is no office-based exemption for attest work. Under section 250d(a)(2)-(3), a no-office firm may perform other (non-attest) services without a firm permit if the work is done through a practice-privileged individual.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Section 250d(a)(1)(A)-(B) requires a permit for 'any firm with an office in the Territory performing attest services' or 'with an office... that uses the title CPA or CPA firm'. Having an office is not a trigger on its own; it is always paired with attest work or use of the CPA title.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition of permit renewal (250d(h)), applicants must undergo peer review no more than once every 3 years, verifying that individuals supervising attest/compilation services meet professional-standards competency requirements.

attest_exemption.citation: CNMI Public Law 13-52 (Accountancy Act of 2002), Section 13(a), (e), with Section 7(a)
attest_exemption.notes: Only a person or firm holding a valid CNMI certificate, permit or registration may issue a report on financial statements (Section 13(a)), and no firm may practice public accountancy or use the CPA title in the CNMI without a CNMI firm permit (Section 13(e)). The Act has no exception for firms without a CNMI office, so attest work there requires a CNMI permit. Tax return preparation and management advisory services fall outside the Section 13(a) prohibition, but a firm holding itself out as a CPA firm while providing them is practicing public accountancy (Section 3(g)) and needs a CNMI permit (Section 13(e)).

physical_office_trigger.notes: A firm holding a CNMI permit must register each of its CNMI offices with the Board (Section 7(d)); that is a condition of the permit rather than a separate trigger. The permit itself is required to practice public accountancy in the CNMI (Sections 7(a), 13(e)).

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: CNMI Public Law 13-52, Section 7(g); NMIAC sections 1-10-710, 1-10-715
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: The Act authorizes the Board to require quality review as a condition of permit renewal (Section 7(g)), and the Board's rules provide that it may require a peer review as a condition of renewed licensing, with an exception for a firm that had a satisfactory peer review under a Board-approved program within the preceding three years (NMIAC sections 1-10-710, 1-10-715). The rules make peer review discretionary rather than a fixed renewal condition; confirm with the Board.

attest_exemption.notes: Oklahoma requires firm registration in three cases: a firm with an Oklahoma office that practices or performs attest work (1); a firm with an Oklahoma office that uses the CPA or PA title (2); or a firm with no Oklahoma office that performs attest work for an Oklahoma client (3), which has its own mobility carve-out under sections 15.12A and 15.30. A firm with no Oklahoma office doing only non-attest work falls under none of these. Section 15.15C states this safe harbor explicitly.

physical_office_trigger.notes: OK office triggers registration via practice-of-public-accounting/attest OR CPA/PA titling; practice of public accounting is defined broadly (includes bookkeeping/tax/advisory), so nearly any active OK office triggers registration in practice.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board may require peer review (not less than every 3 years) as a condition for permit issuance/renewal for attest-performing applicants; also a mandatory element of the no-office attest-mobility exemption.

attest_exemption.notes: No-OR-office firm may perform non-attest services under CPA title without registering via an authorized practitioner (essentially unconditioned); may also perform attest/compilation without registering but under stricter conditions (qualifications + authorized practitioner).

physical_office_trigger.notes: Confirmed verbatim: registration required only if a business organization has an OR office AND (uses CPA title OR performs attest/compilation) -- the 'and' means office alone doesn't independently trigger registration.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms must certify most recent peer review result on initial, reinstatement, and every renewal application; attest/review/compilation firms must enroll in Peer Review.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Pennsylvania office may perform attest and non-attest work under the 'qualified unlicensed entity' mobility exemption (section 5.4) if it practices lawfully in its home state and the work is performed by an individual with practice privileges or a Pennsylvania licensee. For attest work, the individual in charge must be a licensed CPA or PA.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Mobility exemption (qualified unlicensed entity) requires NO PA office; a firm with ANY PA office cannot use it and must be a licensed qualified association regardless of services performed -- unconditional office trigger, cleaner than OK/OR/SC's office+activity formulations.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition for firm renewal license (or initial license for a firm previously practicing elsewhere), board requires peer review unless exempted. Dual-sourced via 49 Pa. Code 11.82(a).

attest_exemption.notes: A firm must hold a Rhode Island permit to provide attest or compilation services, or to use the CPA or CPA-firm title. The statute applies by type of service and title use, so it covers an out-of-state firm with no Rhode Island office.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Confirmed directly: maintaining a physical RI office alone does not trigger the permit requirement -- trigger is service type/title use. A firm that DOES need a permit must then register each RI office.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board requires peer review (not more than once every 3 years) as a condition to permit renewal. Dual-sourced across Justia and direct statute citation.

attest_exemption.notes: No-SC-office firm must register only if performing attest/compilation for an SC client, unless exempt under 40-2-30(I)'s practice-privilege pathway. No-office firm doing ONLY non-attest services isn't captured by any part of section 40-2-40(B), no registration needed.

physical_office_trigger.notes: SC-office firm must register if performing attest/practice of accounting OR using CPA/CPA-firm titling. 'Practice of accounting' broadly defined -- essentially any active SC office triggers registration in practice.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a renewal condition, an applicant engaging in attest/compilation must provide evidence of satisfactory peer review no more than once every 3 years.

attest_exemption.notes: Virginia's firm-licensing statute covers only attest, compilation and financial-statement-preparation services (subsection A); non-attest services fall outside it regardless of office. Under subsection C, a firm whose principal place of business is in another state may provide those covered services without a Virginia license if it is licensed in its home state and the practice-privilege conditions in section 54.1-4411 are met.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Licensure turns on principal place of business in VA combined with attest/compilation/financial-statement-prep services -- not mere office presence, not independent of services performed.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms in the AICPA/board-approved practice-monitoring program scope shall enroll. VA Board's own firm-renewal page independently confirms renewal requires peer-review compliance affirmation.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Washington office may perform attest services in Washington without a firm license only if it meets all four conditions in RCW 18.04.195(1)(a)(ii): (A) it meets the firm ownership requirement in RCW 18.04.195(2)(a); (B) it meets the board's quality assurance review (peer review) requirements; (C) it performs the work through an individual with practice privileges under RCW 18.04.350; and (D) it can lawfully do so in the state where that individual has their principal place of business. Otherwise it must hold a Washington firm license. Compilations and other non-attest services under the CPA title need only conditions (C) and (D) (RCW 18.04.195(1)(b)).

physical_office_trigger.notes: License required for a WA-office firm performing/offering attest or compilation services -- office is coupled to service type, not independent.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms offering/performing attest services must participate in a board-approved peer review program as a condition of renewing each firm license; documentation due by April 30 of renewal year.

attest_exemption.citation: W. Va. Code section 30-9-17(d); section 30-9-16(f)-(g) (mobility attest carve-out)
attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no West Virginia office must hold a section 30-9-17 permit and a section 30-9-19 authorization to perform attest or compilation work for a client whose home office is in West Virginia (section 30-9-16(f)). The only relief is for a lone individual practitioner with substantial equivalency, who may do that work without the firm permit but must still get the 30-9-19 authorization (section 30-9-16(g)); there is no such relief for a firm. A no-office firm not doing attest or compilation work for a West Virginia client may perform other services under the CPA title without a permit, through a practice-privileged individual.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A WV-office firm performing attest/compilation, or using CPA/CPA-firm titling, must hold a permit -- the title-use clause makes an in-state office an independent trigger regardless of specific services once titling is used.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Peer review compliance is a condition of a SEPARATE firm 'authorization' (section 30-9-19) needed to sign attest/compilation reports, distinct from the base firm 'permit' (section 30-9-17) whose own renewal provision doesn't list peer review. Section 30-9-16(g) (the mobility section) names the 30-9-19 authorization (not the 30-9-17 permit) as what an individual practitioner must obtain for WV-home-office attest work, so peer review (a condition of the authorization) binds mobility-privileged individuals performing attest work, not just firms with a permit.

attest_exemption.notes: Wisconsin does not require a certificate or license for services involving accounting skills, such as management advisory services, tax preparation and preparing financial statements without issuing reports on them, or for statements that do not purport to comply with SSARS (section 442.025(6)-(7)). It requires that all attest services a licensed firm provides in Wisconsin be under the charge of a Wisconsin-licensed individual (section 442.08(2)(c)1), and section 442.03 (as amended by 2025 Wisconsin Act 166) bars practice unless 'the person or firm has complied with all of the provisions of this chapter, including licensure'. Its out-of-state mobility provision, section 442.025(4), is written for a person holding a CPA certificate or license from another state, and the statute does not say whether it reaches a firm. Whether a firm with no Wisconsin office may perform attest work without a Wisconsin license is therefore unresolved; confirm with the board.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A person is in practice as a CPA if, among other things, it maintains an office for the transaction of business as a certified public accountant (section 442.02(1m)(b)), and a firm applying for a license must identify each of its Wisconsin offices (section 442.08(2)(a)). Section 442.025(6)-(7) separately exempts certain accounting-skill services, such as tax preparation and financial statements prepared without a report, from licensure, and the statute does not say how the two interact for an office doing only that work.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: The department may not renew a firm's license unless, at least once every 3 years, the firm undergoes peer review (section 442.087(2)).

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Wyoming office may perform attest or compilation services for a client with its home office in Wyoming, and use the CPA firm title, without a permit if it meets the ownership and peer review qualifications of 33-3-132 and works through an individual with practice privileges under 33-3-116(a). Section 33-3-118(b)(xv) separately allows non-attest work on similar terms.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A WY-office firm performing attest/compensated public accounting services, OR using CPA/CPA-firm titling, must hold a permit -- the title clause makes an in-state office an independent trigger whenever CPA titling is used.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Failure to show compliance with practice-monitoring (peer review) programs is grounds for the board to revoke/refuse-to-renew a permit -- structured as disciplinary ground rather than a checklist item. Corroborated by cpaboard.wyo.gov's peer-review page (3.5-year review cycles).

attest_exemption.citation: Haw. Rev. Stat. section 466-7(d); section 466-3; Haw. Admin. Rules section 16-71-24(b)
attest_exemption.notes: No attest-specific carve-out: ALL firms engaged in the (broadly-defined, includes non-attest) practice of public accountancy in Hawaii must hold a firm permit, even with no permanent HI office (they need only designate one principal holding a current HI individual permit). No statutory split exempting non-attest-only out-of-state firms; Hawaii has no firm-level enhanced-mobility statute comparable to IL/IA.

physical_office_trigger.citation: Haw. Admin. Rules section 16-71-24(b)(3)-(4); Haw. Rev. Stat. section 466-7(d)
physical_office_trigger.notes: Not independent in the sense asked -- the firm-permit duty already attaches to ANY firm engaged in HI public accounting regardless of office. A physical HI office changes STRINGENCY (all principals of an office-having firm must individually hold permits, vs. just one principal for a no-office firm), not whether registration is required at all.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Haw. Rev. Stat. section 466-7(b)(5); section 466-34(a); section 466-39
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Directly confirmed: permit renewal requires proof of peer review; every permitted firm must undergo peer review every 3 years; a fail/pass-with-deficiency rating may result in denial/termination/nonrenewal of the permit.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm must be registered with the board to provide attest services or compilation reports, or to use the titles 'CPAs', 'CPA firm', 'LPAs' or 'LPA firm' (section 54-214(1)). Separately, section 54-221(3) bars individuals, including those with Idaho practice privileges, from performing attest services through a business that is not registered under section 54-214 or an equivalent provision of another state's law, which implies attest work through a firm registered only in another state. The statute does not reconcile the two provisions, so whether a firm with no Idaho office must register to perform attest work here is unresolved; confirm with the board.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Registration is triggered by providing attest services or compilation reports, or by using the CPA or LPA firm titles (section 54-214(1)), not by an office as such. A registered firm must also register each of its Idaho offices (section 54-214(3)).

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition of registration renewal, the board by rule requires firms to comply with peer review requirements (section 54-214(6)). Individuals practicing in Idaho under practice privileges follow the peer review requirements of their principal place of business (IDAPA 24.30.01, Rule 207.02).

attest_exemption.notes: No-IL-office firm exempt from licensure for non-attest work via practice-privilege individuals. More permissive than a strict binary: under 'enhanced mobility' (450/5.2(a-5)), a no-office firm can ALSO perform attest work for IL-headquartered clients without a license if peer-review/qualification conditions (450/14.4, 450/16) are met -- license required only if those enhanced-mobility conditions aren't met.

physical_office_trigger.notes: IL office alone isn't unconditional: license required if IL office AND (CPA/CPA-firm titling OR the office performs 'accountancy activities' per 8.05(a)(1), the attest/assurance category specifically). An IL office doing only non-attest work under a non-CPA name wouldn't trigger licensure on plain text.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition of renewal, CPA firms and sole practitioners performing accountancy activities under section 8.05(a)(1) must satisfactorily complete a peer review during the preceding 3-year period, accepted by a Peer Review Administrator, unless exempt under section 16(i) (225 ILCS 450/16(e)).

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Indiana office needs a permit to perform attest work, issue reports, or use the CPA title. A no-office firm doing only non-attest work (no attest reports, no CPA title) needs no permit. Dual-sourced: current codification + Justia historical text.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Office registration is a duty on firms that already must hold/apply for a permit -- the underlying obligation to hold a permit at all comes from the attest/CPA-title trigger, not office presence itself. No provision makes an IN office independently trigger it.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: The board must adopt rules requiring peer review (not more than once every 3 years) as a condition of renewing a permit. 872 IAC 1-6-9 makes peer-review enrollment a renewal condition for firms that do attest work or issue compilation reports, with a narrow exception for firms doing only financial-statement preparation.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Iowa office that does not use the CPA title needs no Iowa permit for any service. Current Iowa Code section 542.20(6)(c) also lets an individual with a practice privilege provide attest services through an out-of-state firm without that firm needing an Iowa permit, if the firm is validly licensed in its home state and meets the ownership and peer-review requirements. An older administrative rule (193A-13.4(2), 2017 text; Iowa's 193A accountancy rules have since been transferred to chapter 481) reads narrower and limits this to review services; the current Code text is broader following a 2017 amendment. Confirm with the board before relying on the broader reading.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Permit required only if IA office AND use of a restricted CPA-style title -- office alone is insufficient on the statute's plain terms.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Iowa Code section 542.7(8)(a); Iowa Admin. Code 193A-13.4(3)
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board by rule requires peer review as a condition of firm-permit renewal, confirmed verbatim in both the Iowa Code and implementing admin rule (at least once every 3 years).

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no New Mexico office does not need a firm permit for attest work (subsection C) or non-attest work (subsection D) if it works through individuals with practice privileges. Attest work carries an additional peer review condition (subsection L/(H)(1)).

physical_office_trigger.notes: Statute conditions the office trigger on attest work or CPA/CPA-firm title use; NM Board's FAQ states plainly a permit is required for any NM office -- functionally the same result in practice. NMSA 61-28B-13(B) itself precisely conditions the trigger on attest work or CPA/CPA-firm title use, never bare office presence alone. The Board's FAQ is informal, non-binding guidance, not an adopted rule -- its looser phrasing is an oversimplification worth knowing about, not a competing legal answer.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: NMSA 1978 section 61-28B-13(L); NMAC Title 16, Ch. 60, Part 4
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition to permit renewal, applicant must undergo peer review per board rules. Confirmed by NMAC 16.60.4.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm must register to perform attest or compilation services, or to use CPA or PA in its name. Education Law 7408(3)(a) requires any firm that uses the title CPA or CPA firm to register, with no exception based on office location. A firm limited to non-attest services may register but is not required to. NYSED's own guidance pages say the same.

physical_office_trigger.citation: NY Education Law section 7408(3); 8 NYCRR section 70.8(d)
physical_office_trigger.notes: Trigger is attest/compilation practice or CPA/PA title use; office count is only a fee variable ($50/office) and disclosure item, not an independent trigger. Confirmed by NYSED guidance.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: NY Education Law section 7410(1); 8 NYCRR section 70.10
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Peer review required as a condition to renewal of firm registration. Non-participating firms file an annual non-participation notice instead.

attest_exemption.notes: No-NC-office firm may perform non-attest services without registering; must file a no-fee Notice of Intent to Practice only if a practice-privilege individual performs an audit/SAS engagement, SSAE examination, or PCAOB-standard engagement. Dual-sourced via NC Board's own mobility page.

physical_office_trigger.notes: No-permit mobility exemption applies only to a firm with no NC principal place of business/office; NC Board guidance confirms any NC office removes exemption eligibility.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firm desiring to obtain/maintain registration must offer satisfactory evidence of peer review compliance. Reviews valid a minimum of 3 years, subject to board-ordered remedial action.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no North Dakota office may perform any public accountancy service, including attest, without a firm permit if it works through an individual with practice privileges. A North Dakota office, not the type of service, is what triggers the permit requirement.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Any firm with an ND office practicing public accountancy or using CPA/LPA titling must hold a permit. Confirmed by ND Board's own Firms page.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board has permissive authority to require practice reviews (not more than once every 3 years) as a renewal condition; ND Board's site confirms this is implemented for firms performing attest services.

attest_exemption.citation: Ohio Rev. Code section 4701.04(A); section 4701.14; Ohio Admin. Code 4701-13-02
attest_exemption.notes: Section 4701.04(A) requires registration of a public accounting firm 'located in this state'. Ohio Admin. Code 4701-13-02(C) requires any public accounting firm that performs or offers engagements resulting in an attest report to notify the board within ninety days and register as a peer review firm 'pursuant to section 4701.04', with no location qualifier. Read one way, that phrase imports 4701.04's location limit; read the other, it creates a separate duty for out-of-state firms. The text does not settle which; confirm with the board.

physical_office_trigger.notes: No public accounting firm located in Ohio may practice without registering; practice of public accounting is defined broadly (includes attest and, by board rule, other accounting-skill services for CPA-affiliated firms).

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Ohio Rev. Code section 4701.04(F); Ohio Admin. Code 4701-13-02
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition for initial/renewal registration, the board requires peer review by rule unless an exception in division (J) applies. OAC 4701-13-02 requires documentation of approved peer review by the October 31 renewal deadline.

ohio.source_disagreement: Ohio Rev. Code section 4701.04(A) requires registration only for a firm located in Ohio, but Ohio Admin. Code 4701-13-02(C) requires any firm that performs engagements resulting in an attest report to notify the board within ninety days and register as a peer review firm, without a stated location limit.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Montana office may use the CPA firm title without registering, and may offer attest services and compilations in Montana if it complies with Montana's peer review and firm ownership qualifications, works through an individual with practice privileges under section 37-50-325, and has practice privileges that include attest and compilation services in the state of its principal place of business (section 37-50-335(4)(a)). Confirm with the board how a firm that does not meet those conditions may proceed.

physical_office_trigger.notes: All firms that establish or maintain offices in Montana for the practice of public accounting must register annually with the department (section 37-50-335(1)).

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Admin. R. Mont. 24.201.1103; 24.201.2410; Mont. Code Ann. section 37-50-335(4)(a)
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Registered firms that perform audits, reviews or compilations, SSAE examination, review or agreed-upon-procedures engagements, or PCAOB-standards engagements for non-issuers must enroll in a board-approved peer review program (ARM 24.201.1103(1)). Failing to comply with the peer review rules, or receiving a fail report or a second or subsequent pass-with-deficiency report, may be cause for disciplinary action (ARM 24.201.2410). For a firm with no Montana office, compliance with Montana's peer review qualifications is a condition of practicing without registering (section 37-50-335(4)(a)).

attest_exemption.citation: 288 Neb. Admin. Code ch. 11, section 005.01; ch. 3, section 001; Neb. Rev. Stat. section 1-125.01(4)
attest_exemption.notes: Admin rule + Board guidance require firm registration for ANY public accounting work for an NE client, attest or not -- no clean no-office/non-attest exemption. Caveat: firm-registration statute is permissive ('may register') and individual-mobility statute (section 1-125.01) ties routing-through-a-permitted-firm specifically to attestation, creating internal tension with the stricter rule/guidance (resolved in favor of the rule). Section 1-125.01(4): 'Any person who exercises the practice privilege afforded under this section and who, for any entity with its home office in this state, performs attestation services, may only do so through a firm or an affiliated entity which holds a permit issued under section 1-136.' This conditions firm-permit routing on attestation specifically and is silent on non-attest work -- it doesn't affirmatively exempt non-attest work from all registration, but its silence is genuinely readable either way. Unlike Arizona (which had an express 'except as provided in' cross-reference), nothing in 1-125.01 or the admin rule itself resolves the silence one way or the other.

physical_office_trigger.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. section 1-135; 288 Neb. Admin. Code ch. 10, section 001
physical_office_trigger.notes: Each office established/maintained in NE for public accountancy practice must be registered annually, independent of services performed. Dual-sourced: statute + near-identical implementing rule.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. section 1-153; 288 Neb. Admin. Code ch. 13, section 004.01/.03(B)
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board may restrict permits based on peer review results; attest/compilation firms must furnish peer review evidence with renewal application; preparation-only firms exempt. Dual-sourced.

nebraska.source_disagreement: Attest-exemption question only: the individual-mobility statute (Neb. Rev. Stat. 1-125.01(4)) conditions firm-permit routing on attestation specifically and is silent on non-attest work; the administrative rule (288 NAC ch. 11 section 005.01) requires registration for ANY public accounting work, attest or not, with no such carve-out. Genuinely unresolved by the statute's own text -- the stricter administrative rule is used as the primary answer, a conservative reading, not a forced resolution of the tension.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Nevada office that is in good standing in its home state is treated as a Nevada CPA firm 'for all purposes' and is exempt from registration, including for attest work. The only condition is that the firm has no Nevada office.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A firm with an NV office must register if it performs attest/compilation, practices public accounting, or uses the CPA designation -- office presence removes the mobility exemption, then combines with any of those triggers. Dual-sourced: NRS text + NAC 628.010(3)(c).

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Renewal provisions condition renewal only on fee payment and CE -- none reference peer review. Peer review is a separate mandatory-enrollment duty enforced through discipline for noncompliance, not framed as a renewal precondition. Triple-sourced (three independent renewal provisions all omit peer review).

attest_exemption.notes: No-office firm doing non-attest services under CPA title doesn't need a permit via practice-privileged individuals; no-office firm doing attest for an NH-home-office client generally needs a permit unless it separately qualifies for a narrow mobility exemption (ownership/experience quals, practice-privilege individuals only, home-state licensure). Second source (Ac 302.05(a)-(b)) confirms the permit requirement ties to assurance/compilation for NH-home-office clients. Ac 302.05, titled "CPA Firm Permit Requirements" (post-renumbering, formerly Ac 301.10), subsection (b): "Each CPA firm seeking a permit to practice as a CPA firm in NH that provides assurance services or compilation services for a client having its home office in NH shall..."

physical_office_trigger.notes: Office-holding firm using CPA/CPA-firm designation needs a permit regardless of service mix; office-holding firms doing attest/compilation also need one. De facto independent trigger for essentially any NH-office accounting firm. Ac 303.05, titled "CPA Firms" (post-renumbering, formerly Ac 302.07), subsection (c): "The applicant CPA firm shall demonstrate, pursuant to RSA 309-B:8, I, that it has or will have a physical presence in NH by a date certain..."

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board shall require peer review as a condition to renewal of permits; rule requires a signed Peer Review Affidavit with each application/renewal, issuing only a time-limited conditional permit if the most recent review was adverse/qualified. Dual-sourced (Ac 302.07 "Affidavit for Peer Review" and Ac 303.05(g)-(i)), unusually explicit.

attest_exemption.notes: Registration required only if NJ office + attest work, NJ office + CPA titling, or (no NJ office) offering attest services to NJ clients -- unless narrow practice-privilege conditions are met. No-office firm doing only non-attest work may operate unregistered via practice-privileged individuals. Dual-sourced: statute + implementing rule, agreeing.

physical_office_trigger.notes: NJ office alone isn't independent: registration required only if the NJ office does attest work OR uses CPA/Certified-Public-Accountant titling there. A bare NJ office doing only non-attest work under a non-CPA name wouldn't be forced to register on the statutory text.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: The triennial registration application must include peer-review compliance forms, and Peer Review Program participation is mandatory for firms doing attest or accounting-and-auditing work (firms doing only compilations without a report are exempt). Under N.J.S.A. 45:2B-59(a)(3) the board may refuse to renew a registration for failure to maintain compliance with the requirements for renewal, which include the participation mandate in N.J.A.C. 13:29-5.4(a). Separately, 45:2B-59(c)(1) lets the board order a peer review as a sanction in a disciplinary case. No single sentence says renewal is refused for missing peer review; that follows from these provisions together. Confirm with the board.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm may practice in Colorado without registering with the board if the practice is incident to its regular practice outside Colorado (section 12-100-117(2)(a)(II)), and board Rule 1.14(B)(2) applies this to a firm holding an active firm license or registration in another state. Section 12-100-116(1)(a)(III) lifts the registration requirement for audit and attest work by a firm practicing under section 12-100-117(2). Confirm with the board that your engagement qualifies.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A firm practicing in Colorado must register unless the section 12-100-117(2)(a)(II) exemption for practice incident to regular practice outside Colorado applies (section 12-100-114(1), as amended by SB 26-076 in 2026), and each resident manager in charge of a Colorado office must be a Colorado CPA (section 12-100-114(1)(d)). Our reading: a standing Colorado office is unlikely to qualify as practice incident to out-of-state practice, though neither the statute nor the board's rules say so expressly. Confirm with the board.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: The board cannot renew the registration of a firm that issues attest or compilation reports unless the firm has attested to undergoing a peer review (Rule 1.15(D)(3); section 12-100-114(7)).

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Connecticut office needs a permit to do attest work for a client headquartered in Connecticut. A no-office firm doing only non-attest work may use the CPA title without a permit if it meets quality-review requirements and works through a practice-privilege individual. Dual-sourced: statute + portal.ct.gov firm-permit page.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Permit required for CT office + attest work, or CT office + CPA titling -- near-universal trigger in practice since most firms use CPA titling. Dual-sourced.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Quality review every 3 years as a condition of permit renewal; annual waiver available for firms attesting no attest/financial-reporting work. Dual-sourced.

attest_exemption.citation: 24 Del. C. sections 109(c), 111(b); 24 Del. Admin. Code 100 section 10.1
attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Delaware office does not need a Delaware firm permit, for attest or non-attest work, if it practices through an individual with Delaware practice privileges.

physical_office_trigger.citation: 24 Del. C. section 111(a); 24 Del. Admin. Code 100 sections 10.2, 10.3
physical_office_trigger.notes: Any firm with a DE office engaged in public accounting practice must obtain/maintain a permit -- unconditional on service type. Dual-sourced, statute + rule verbatim agreement.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: 24 Del. C. section 111(m); 24 Del. Admin. Code 100 sections 10.4, 10.6, 10.12.2.1-3
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board-approved peer review enrollment required as a condition of permit renewal for attest/compilation firms (eff. 2017-07-01); also a condition of initial issuance. Firms doing only SSARS prep (no attest/compilation) exempt from enrollment. Dual-sourced.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no DC office must register to perform attest services for a DC-headquartered client. The same firm may perform non-attest services without registering if the work is done through a practice-privileged individual.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Not truly independent: registration required for a DC-office firm only when it also performs attest services or uses CPA/CPA-firm titling. No requirement for a DC-office firm doing only non-attest work under a non-CPA name.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: 17 DCMR section 2548; renewal mechanics at 17 DCMR section 2547
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms performing audits, reviews, compilations or other SSAE/SAS/SSARS engagements must enroll in and complete a board-approved peer review. We did not find an explicit statement in section 2547 that peer review is a condition of renewal; that reading follows from the overall rules. Confirm with the board.

attest_exemption.citation: Fla. Stat. section 473.3101(1)(a)-(c), with section 473.3141(4) and section 473.302(8)(a)
attest_exemption.notes: Licensure required only if: FL office + attest/CPA titling, OR no FL office + attest work for a FL-headquartered client (with a no-notice mobility pathway if 473.309-qualified + peer-review enrolled). No-office firms doing only non-attest work aren't addressed at all -- no trigger. Dual-sourced: statute + DBPR Mobility FAQ.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Strictly FL office + (attest OR CPA titling), but near-universal in practice since nearly all firms use CPA titling. Dual-sourced: statute + DBPR Mobility FAQ, no service-type carve-out for an FL office.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Fla. Admin. Code r. 61H1-39.005(2)-(3)(a); Fla. Stat. section 473.3125(4)
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms performing 473.3125(4)-covered services must enroll in board-approved peer review prior to renewal or initial licensure. Dual-sourced: statute + admin rule.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Georgia office is never exempt for audits or other engagements under SAS, SSAE or PCAOB standards. Compilations and reviews are exempt only if the firm meets Georgia's firm ownership requirement, is enrolled in peer review, and performs the work through a substantial-equivalency individual. Other non-attest services are exempt if performed through a substantial-equivalency individual. Dual-sourced: statute+rule + GA Board Statement of Policy No. 11.

physical_office_trigger.notes: GA office practicing public accounting or using CPA/CPA-firm titling requires licensure, untethered to service mix. Dual-sourced: statute + GA Board Statement of Policy No. 14 (offices register within 60 days of opening).

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms issuing attest/compilation reports must submit evidence of satisfactory peer review within 36 months preceding license expiration; noncompliant firms barred from licensure/renewal. Dual-sourced: statute+rule + GA Board Statement of Policy No. 20.
